ordered_attempts.question_stem: Two bulbs in series with ammeters A1, A2, A3.
ordered_attempts.student_response: A1 = 1.2A, A2 = 0.8A, A3 = 0.4A. Bulb 1 consumes some current, and Bulb 2 consumes the rest.

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Three identical resistors in series with ammeters before and after each resistor.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Current drops from 3A to 2A after the first resistor, then drops to 1A after the second resistor.

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Diagnostic Probe: If we swap the order of a 10-ohm and 2-ohm resistor in series, what happens to current?
ordered_attempts.student_response: The first resistor in line will always get the most current because current is depleted as it travels.

evidence_summary: Q1: Student explicitly asserts current consumed by bulbs sequentially
Q2: Replicated linear current drop across 3-resistor series configuration
Q3: Probe confirmed student ignores resistance value and relies strictly on spatial sequence order

topic: Electricity: Parallel Resistance and Battery Behavior

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Adding a 3-ohm resistor in parallel across a 6-ohm resistor powered by 12V battery.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Total current stays 2A because the 12V battery always outputs 2A.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

ordered_attempts.question_stem: If we connect 5 more resistors in parallel, does the battery current change?
ordered_attempts.student_response: No, battery current is fixed by the battery.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-ELEC-002: Battery as Constant Current Source

evidence_summary: Q1: Asserts battery delivers constant current despite branch addition
Q2: Reaffirms invariant battery current under multi-branch load

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Cannot see blackboard clearly at 5m, reads book clearly at 25cm. Name defect and corrective lens.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Myopia, corrected with convex lens so distant letters are magnified.
ordered_attempts.individual_diagnosis: MISC-EYE-001: Vision Defect Corrective Lens Inversion

ordered_attempts.question_stem: Simulation showing myopic eye over-converging rays in front of retina.
ordered_attempts.student_response: Oh! The eye lens is already bending the rays too much. A convex lens makes it bend even earlier! We need a concave lens to diverge them back onto the retina.

ordered_attempts.question_stem: A patient cannot see objects beyond 1.5m. What lens power and type should be prescribed?
ordered_attempts.student_response: Diverging concave lens of focal length -1.5m, power P = -0.67 D.

evidence_summary: Q1: Inverted lens prescription based on magnification analogy
Step 2: Ray trace simulation clarified over-convergence
Step 3: Correct numerical prescription and concave lens choice
